Chapter 7: Rewriting the Stories We Tell Ourselves
Have you ever noticed the story playing in the back of your mind? We all have one—a quiet narrative about who we are, what we’re worth, and how the world sees us. Sometimes, those stories lift us up. But more often, you might find they’re laced with self-doubt or harsh criticism.
Let me share an example. Picture a woman who’s spent years feeling overlooked at work. After a while, she starts to believe she just isn’t capable. Every little mistake becomes proof: “I’m not good enough.” And when a new opportunity pops up, she freezes—convinced she’ll fall short.
Then, a friend steps in. Gently, they challenge her story, reminding her of all the times she’s succeeded, all the strengths she’s shown. Suddenly, the script in her mind starts to shift. She begins to see herself in a different light.
Or think about a man raised in a home full of criticism. He grows up expecting rejection in every relationship. Even minor disagreements—he takes them as proof he’s unlovable. But with time, and some real effort, he realizes: his old story isn’t the only truth. Supported by others, he starts to rewrite his script, little by little. He decides to believe he’s worthy of love and respect.
Most of us don’t even notice these stories running in the background. They shape our reactions, our choices—almost like a silent director calling the shots. But here’s the thing: when you start paying attention, you can actually challenge those old scripts.
It begins by catching those familiar phrases that pop up in tough moments. Maybe it’s “I always mess up,” or “No one cares,” or “I’ll never change.” But those aren’t facts—they’re just beliefs. And beliefs can be changed.
Here’s where faith can make a difference. It offers a new kind of story—one built on love, acceptance, and hope. Instead of letting old mistakes or harsh opinions define you, you’re invited to see yourself through a lens of grace. That doesn’t erase the past, but it does lay down a new foundation for what’s ahead.
Changing your story isn’t easy. Those old narratives are stubborn, and setbacks happen. But every time you choose a kinder word for yourself, every time you remember your true worth, the story shifts just a bit. Over time, that new narrative can grow stronger—guiding your choices and shaping your relationships.
And remember, this journey isn’t about pretending everything’s perfect. It’s about being honest—about struggles, about growth, and about the real possibility of change. In the end, the story that matters most is the one that leads you toward hope, healing, and genuine connection.
